note: Manually-refreshed research digest compiled from public news sources, including regional/vernacular press, local TV channels and YouTube ground reports where available. Not a live news-wire feed — update this file (or re-run research) to refresh. Built for Meesho 3P logistics capacity planning (Delhivery · Shadowfax · Xpressbees): LM/FM manifestation, non-adherence hotspots, and serviceability-loss tracking. Not an official Meesho product.

Anant Chaturdashi / Ganpati Visarjan (Sep 25): mass immersion processions — major LM disruption in Mumbai, Pune, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Delhi
Gandhi Jayanti (Oct 2): pan-India public holiday, 1-day dispatch/pickup slip expected nationwide
Guru Ram Das Ji Parkash Gurpurab (Oct 9): Punjab gurdwara gatherings, localized route congestion
Sharad Navratri (Oct 11-19): pan-India garba/pandal crowds — expect evening route congestion in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Delhi-NCR
Mahalaya Amavasya / Sarva Pitru Amavasya (Oct 10): final day of Pitru Paksha, precedes Sharad Navratri — marks transition into peak festive-season LM surge nationally
Durga Puja (Oct 16-20): West Bengal/Odisha/Assam pandal crowds & processions — expect major LM slowdown in Kolkata/Bhubaneswar/Guwahati
Dussehra/Vijayadashami (Oct 20): pan-India Ravana-dahan processions, route closures likely in city centers
Maharishi Valmiki Jayanti (Oct 26): regional holiday in Punjab/Haryana/Delhi, minor local market closures
Karva Chauth (Oct 29): North India evening market rush — expect last-mile delays 5-9pm in Delhi-NCR/Punjab/UP
Guru Granth Sahib Parkash Gurpurab (Nov 5): gurdwara processions in Punjab/Delhi-NCR, minor local route congestion
All Saints' & All Souls' Day (Nov 1-2): Goa/Kerala/Northeast Christian community observance, minor local impact
Diwali (Nov 8): peak-season demand surge + multi-day shop closures pan-India — plan buffer stock & extended SLA nationwide
Govardhan Puja (Nov 10): North India regional holiday, local market closures
Bhai Dooj (Nov 11): pan-India family-visit travel rush, minor LM slowdown
Chhath Puja (Nov 13-16, main day Nov 15): Bihar/UP/Jharkhand ghat gatherings — expect serviceability dip in Patna/Varanasi/Ranchi belt
Guru Nanak Gurpurab (Nov 24): Punjab-wide processions/holiday — expect statewide LM slowdown
Christmas (Dec 25): Goa/Kerala/Northeast peak demand & multi-day closures — plan buffer stock in Christian-majority belts

alerts.title: Manipur: Kangpokpi villagers released but UNC's NH-2/37/202/102A economic blockade remains active into its third week
alerts.summary: A CRPF CoBRA unit's arrest of six Kholen/Kholep villagers near Chawangkining triggered violent protests in Kangpokpi and Motbung on Sep 20-21 — protesters torched a CRPF vehicle, dug up NH-2 with JCB machines and pelted security convoys with stones; tear gas was used to disperse the crowds. The six detained villagers have since been released and authorities describe the immediate flashpoint as 'under control', but the United Naga Council's indefinite economic blockade of NH-2, NH-37, NH-202 and NH-102A remains in force since Sep 8-9 with no talks breakthrough, and unrest has spread to nearby settlements including Saikul, Sapormeina, Gamgiphai and Taphou.
alerts.impact: Critical serviceability loss across Manipur — all four major highway arteries remain under active blockade despite the immediate flashpoint cooling. Flag Imphal Valley and border-district pincodes non-serviceable/high-delay; use air-cargo or alternate routing where feasible; do not commit SLA promises anywhere in Manipur until the UNC blockade de-escalates.

alerts.title: Manipur: fresh 48-hour statewide bandh from midnight Sep 26 escalates after Manipur University raid detains 89 students, 6 faculty
alerts.summary: AMSU, MSF, KSA, SUK, DESAM and AIMS have called a 48-hour statewide bandh from midnight Sep 26 after police/CRPF conducted an overnight raid on Manipur University's hostel (Sep 20-21), detaining 89 students and 6 faculty. This follows an already-lapsed 24-hour NRFM bandh on Sep 21 over the 1949 Merger Agreement, which shut shops, offices and public transport in valley districts with essential services exempted.
alerts.impact: Pre-position stock and communicate SLA delays to sellers ahead of the Sep 26 midnight start; expect a full valley-wide LM/FM shutdown for 48 hours (through Sep 28) layered on top of the ongoing NH blockades and statewide internet shutdown.

alerts.title: Manipur: statewide mobile internet shutdown remains in force since Sep 21 following Manipur University raid
alerts.summary: Mobile internet has been suspended statewide since Sep 21 following the Manipur University hostel raid and student arrests, compounding the existing UNC highway blockade and the upcoming Sep 26 bandh call. No restoration has been reported as of Sep 22.
alerts.impact: OTP-based delivery confirmation, seller app access and rider app connectivity will be degraded statewide — pre-brief LM/FM teams on offline delivery workflows and expect manifestation/tracking gaps until the shutdown lifts.

alerts.title: Manipur/Assam: 800+ goods trucks and fuel tankers stranded at Jiribam and Jirighat as CRPF escort-convoy shortage compounds NH-37 landslides
alerts.summary: Roughly 420 trucks at Jiribam and 350 at Jirighat (Manipur-Assam border) are stranded because CRPF is running only about one escort convoy every two days instead of the usual daily pace, on top of landslide damage near Barak-Sibilong and the Irang bridge on NH-37. NH-37 is currently the only functioning supply corridor into Manipur since NH-2 (Imphal-Dimapur) remains disrupted by the Kangpokpi unrest.
alerts.impact: Direct FM/LM linehaul risk for any freight routed through the Northeast corridor — build 3-4 day buffer for goods bound to/from Manipur via NH-37 and pre-position stock on the Assam side (Silchar/Jiribam) until escort frequency normalizes.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh: 51 roads remain blocked statewide, Mandi (24) still worst-hit; Parvati Valley slope stays unstable with fresh vehicle-damaging slides
alerts.summary: 51 roads remain blocked across Himachal Pradesh — Mandi (24), Kangra (10) and Kullu (9) remain worst-affected, with Una, Sirmaur, Lahaul-Spiti and Shimla each reporting a handful. A fresh landslide at Kukdiglu on the Chailchowk-Tattapani road (Mandi) halted traffic for three hours on Sep 18. Separately, the Manikaran-Barshaini stretch in Kullu's Parvati Valley remains persistently unstable — a fresh slide at Ghatigad damaged another vehicle days after the initial major slide, and no source confirms the road is fully cleared as of Sep 22. Light-to-moderate rain is forecast to continue through Sep 22 before tapering.
alerts.impact: Mandi/Kullu/Kangra hub-to-last-mile routes still face intermittent closures — maintain buffer stock at Mandi and Kullu hubs and keep alternate routing ready through the week; treat Parvati Valley (Manikaran-Barshaini) as non-serviceable given repeated fresh slides, not a one-off closure.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh: Manikaran-Barshaini road (Parvati Valley, Kullu) still not confirmed cleared — repeat slides at Ghatigad keep damaging vehicles
alerts.summary: A large landslide blocked the Manikaran-Barshaini road in Kullu district's Parvati Valley, stranding travellers and cutting connectivity to upper-valley villages including Kasol and Barshaini. The stretch remains volatile — a subsequent slide at Ghatigad damaged another car days later — and no source confirms full restoration as of Sep 22.
alerts.impact: Flag Parvati Valley (Manikaran-Barshaini-Kasol) pincodes non-serviceable for LM/FM until the road is confirmed cleared; route via alternate Kullu-valley approaches where available.

alerts.title: J&K: Doda-Bhaderwah road still blocked at Chalnai village after Sep 19 landslide, no reopening confirmed
alerts.summary: The Doda-Bhaderwah road remains blocked near Chalnai village after a landslide on September 19 halted vehicular movement between the two towns. Debris-clearance machinery remains engaged, but no source confirms full restoration as of Sep 22 — treat the road as still disrupted.
alerts.impact: Route watch — Doda-Bhaderwah corridor: hold non-essential LM/linehaul via Chalnai until the road is confirmed cleared, and route via alternate approach roads where available for Bhaderwah-side pincodes.

alerts.title: J&K: NH-44 Ramban-Banihal stretch under daytime-only advisory; hazmat/tanker vehicles barred 7am-3pm amid widening work
alerts.summary: Very slow traffic continues on NH-44 between Ramban and Banihal due to NHAI widening work at Digdole-Khooni Nallah. Authorities are restricting inflammable-cargo tankers to a 7am-3pm window and advising daytime-only travel, citing breakdowns and landslide-prone stretches. NH-44 is the primary highway corridor for goods movement between Jammu and the Kashmir valley.
alerts.impact: Build extra transit time into First/Last Mile linehaul between Jammu and Srinagar via Ramban-Banihal; schedule hazmat-adjacent shipments within the 7am-3pm window and avoid dispatching time-sensitive shipments through this corridor at night.

alerts.title: J&K: LeT logistics module busted in Rajouri's Chassana/Reasi-Shopian belt — network described as contained, probe widening
alerts.summary: Police confirmed three OGWs arrested (Sep 15-19) facilitated terrorist movement across the Rajouri-Reasi-Shopian belt, linked to the 2023 Chassana encounter; a pistol, grenades and an IED were recovered. The immediate cell is described as neutralized, though the wider probe continues. No curfews, checkpoints or transport restrictions have resulted from this case as of Sep 22.
alerts.impact: Watch item — Rajouri/Reasi/Shopian/Poonch belt pincodes: monitor for any follow-on movement restrictions or network curbs; no current LM/FM action needed but keep contingency routing in mind for this corridor.

alerts.title: J&K: ISI spy network arrest in Kathua — accused installed SIM-enabled CCTV to feed live army-route footage to Pakistan
alerts.summary: Police in Kathua arrested Mohd Aman on Sep 21 for allegedly installing SIM-enabled CCTV cameras to transmit live army-movement footage to Pakistan — a case distinct from the Rajouri LeT module. No transport or movement restrictions have followed as of Sep 22.
alerts.impact: Watch item only — no current LM/FM restriction in the Kathua belt; monitor for any follow-on security cordon that could affect border-district routing.

alerts.title: Uttarakhand: Pithoragarh bans night traffic 6pm-6am on Ghat Bend stretch of NH-9 for 15 days after repeated stonefall injuries
alerts.summary: Continuous stonefall at Ghat Bend on the Pithoragarh-Tanakpur NH-9 injured commercial-vehicle passengers, prompting a 6pm-6am vehicle movement ban for at least 15 days (through roughly Oct 2). NH officials plan permanent slope treatment across a 200m stretch; the long-term protection plan has since been submitted to NHAI/GoI. Separately, roughly 22 connecting motor roads remain closed in neighbouring Chamoli district after earlier-September rain, though the Badrinath Highway itself is open.
alerts.impact: FM/LM movement on the Pithoragarh-Tanakpur axis must be scheduled strictly within the 6am-6pm window until at least early October; build in buffer time and avoid time-critical dispatches through this stretch during active rain. Chamoli hub dispatches should verify individual village-road status before dispatch given the still-elevated closed-road count.

alerts.title: Uttar Pradesh: flood situation stabilizing across 26 districts, but IMD flags fresh heavy-rain spell for Sep 25-26
alerts.summary: 17,544 people evacuated across 26 UP districts (Ayodhya, Ballia, Barabanki, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Kanpur, Lakhimpur Kheri, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Bahraich and others) remains the latest confirmed figure, with Ganga/Ghaghra still above the danger mark at Ballia and Bahraich. No fresh evacuation surge has been reported since, giving a temporary lull, but IMD's latest bulletin flags a renewed heavy-rain spell for UP, Haryana and Delhi around Sep 25-26 tied to the Bay of Bengal system moving inland after its Sep 23-24 landfall.
alerts.impact: Sustain existing contingency routing for hubs in Gorakhpur, Ayodhya, Varanasi, Prayagraj and the Bahraich/Sharda Barrage belt through the current lull, but pre-position buffer stock again ahead of the Sep 25-26 spell.

alerts.title: Punjab: PRTC/PUNBUS/Roadways contract-worker chakka jam deferred to Sep 24 pending Transport Minister meeting; ~2,700 buses at stake
alerts.summary: Contract workers of Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC had announced a complete chakka jam from Sep 22, alleging the government failed to resolve demands despite repeated meetings over four years; the union has now confirmed it will continue bus operations until its next meeting with the government on Sep 24. If that meeting with the Transport Minister fails, an indefinite strike affecting roughly 2,700 buses and 5,500 drivers/conductors could follow. Their core demand is ending the outsourcing system in favour of direct department contracts.
alerts.impact: No disruption currently. Flag Sep 24 as a hard checkpoint — pre-stage alternate transport for Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Amritsar and Patiala FM/LM routes ahead of that date in case talks fail.

alerts.title: Punjab: Kisan Mazdoor Morcha farmers continue rail-roko at Gurdaspur, Amritsar, Moga, Firozepur, Sangrur over MSP demand; trains diverted via Tarn Taran
alerts.summary: Since around Sep 15, farmers under the Kisan Mazdoor Morcha have blocked rail tracks at five Punjab locations — Gurdaspur, Amritsar, Moga, Firozepur and Sangrur — demanding legal MSP guarantees on basmati, mustard, potatoes, moong and maize, plus debt relief and withdrawal of the land pooling policy. Talks between farmer leader Pandher and district/IG Border Range officials have not resolved the standoff; trains continue to be diverted via Tarn Taran.
alerts.impact: Rail-linked freight through Amritsar, Moga, Firozepur and Sangrur corridors faces continued delays/diversions — prefer road linehaul for these hubs until the blockade lifts.

alerts.title: Rajasthan: heavy rain/60kmph-wind alert for Jhunjhunu, Tonk, Ajmer, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Barmer and 7 other districts even as monsoon withdrawal begins
alerts.summary: IMD has issued a genuine heavy rain, thunderstorm and 60kmph gusty-wind alert for Jhunjhunu, Tonk, Ajmer, Chittorgarh, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Barmer, Bharatpur, Sikar, Pratapgarh, Bhilwara and Pali districts of Rajasthan for Sep 21-22, even as the monsoon begins formal withdrawal from western Rajasthan. By contrast, Delhi-NCR and UP are only seeing light-to-moderate isolated rain on Sep 22 with no formal warning — the bigger UP/Delhi/Haryana spell has been pushed to Sep 25-26.
alerts.impact: Prioritize buffer planning for the named Rajasthan districts through Sep 22-23; Delhi-NCR/UP FM/LM operations should see only minor, isolated rain-linked delays until the Sep 25-26 spell arrives.

alerts.title: Nationwide: petrol/diesel steady but sit at multi-city highs; commercial LPG and CNG remain elevated as crude trades near $102/bbl on Strait of Hormuz disruption
alerts.summary: As of Sep 22, retail petrol/diesel prices are holding steady but at multi-city highs — Delhi ₹102.12/₹95.20, Mumbai ₹111.21/₹97.83, Hyderabad ₹115.69/₹103.82, Chennai ₹107.76/₹99.55 per litre. No fresh petrol/diesel hike was recorded today. Commercial 19kg LPG cylinders remain at the elevated ₹2,747.50 (Delhi) level reached after the Sep 1 hike (cumulative +₹669/32.2% since April); domestic 14.2kg LPG is steady at ₹942. CNG remains up to ₹2/kg higher than a year ago in Delhi and Mumbai as crude trades near $102/barrel amid ongoing Strait of Hormuz-linked disruption.
alerts.impact: No new cost shock today, but factor sustained high CNG/commercial-LPG costs into last-mile fleet fuel budgeting nationwide, especially for CNG-fleet-heavy metro hubs (Delhi-NCR, Mumbai); monitor for further crude-driven hikes if Strait of Hormuz tensions persist.

alerts.title: Mumbai: heavy-vehicle bans on JVLR, NH-66 and Vasai-Virar confirmed for Anant Chaturdashi visarjan, Sep 25-26
alerts.summary: Traffic police have confirmed timings for the final Ganesh immersion: JVLR heavy-vehicle ban from 10:00 AM Sep 25 to 12:00 PM Sep 26; NH-66 (Mumbai-Goa highway) ban on vehicles ≥16 tonnes from 08:00 hrs Sep 25 to 20:00 hrs Sep 26; and a Vasai-Virar zone (Vasai, Nalasopara, Naigaon) restriction from 2 PM to midnight on immersion days. LPG, milk, medicine, fuel and JNPT/Jaigarh port carriers are exempted.
alerts.impact: Plan FM/LM linehaul on JVLR, NH-66 and Vasai-Virar corridors around these windows; pre-position or reroute non-exempt heavy vehicles via alternate routes to avoid multi-hour idling during peak immersion procession hours.

alerts.title: Maharashtra: Raghuveer Ghat (Khed taluka, Ratnagiri) landslide severs 15-20 villages; second Khed slide traps two
alerts.summary: A landslide at Raghuveer Ghat (Khed taluka, Ratnagiri) has severed road connectivity to 15-20 villages, and a separate landslide elsewhere in Khed taluka trapped two people; district authorities issued a yellow alert and shut schools. IMD warns of further isolated heavy rain with 30-50 kmph winds over Sindhudurg and Ratnagiri on Sep 22-23, raising fresh slope-stability concerns on this already-damaged ghat, which had earlier been closed to tourists into August.
alerts.impact: Flag Raghuveer Ghat (Ratnagiri-Satara link) and the 15-20 cut-off Khed taluka villages as non-serviceable/high-delay; monitor NH-66 through Sindhudurg/Ratnagiri for possible fresh blockages through Sep 23.

alerts.title: Maharashtra: yellow alert for 26 districts widens to orange for Dhule, Nandurbar, Nashik ghats and Vidarbha through Sep 25
alerts.summary: IMD's yellow alert spans ~26 districts — Palghar, Thane, Mumbai, Raigad, Ratnagiri, Pune, Nagpur and others — with an orange alert added for Dhule, Nandurbar and the Nashik ghat sections plus several Vidarbha districts. Marathwada is expected to see fairly widespread rain intensifying to very/extremely heavy spells Sep 23-24, driven by the Bay of Bengal system tracking toward Odisha-AP.
alerts.impact: Expect intermittent LM delivery delays and FM pickup slippage across Mumbai/Thane/Pune/Nagpur hubs; build in extra buffer for Nashik-ghat, Dhule-Nandurbar and Marathwada/Vidarbha linehaul through Sep 25.

alerts.title: Gujarat: yellow alert for Dwarka, Jamnagar, Porbandar, Junagadh, Rajkot as monsoon withdrawal stalls over Saurashtra-Kutch
alerts.summary: IMD has issued a yellow alert for heavy rain and gusty winds in five Saurashtra districts — Dwarka, Jamnagar, Porbandar, Junagadh and Rajkot — as a revived coastal low delays monsoon withdrawal from the region. Withdrawal has begun from western Rajasthan but Saurashtra-Kutch remains under active flash-flood watch, with fishermen warned off the Arabian Sea coast.
alerts.impact: Expect rain-linked slowdowns for FM pickups in Rajkot, Jamnagar and Junagadh belts; downgrade this watch only once monsoon withdrawal is confirmed complete over the region.

alerts.title: Gujarat: Ahmedabad's Mithakhali underpass shut for 102 minutes as moderate rain reflows five chronic waterlogging spots
alerts.summary: Renewed rain on Sep 19-21 waterlogged Ahmedabad's chronic choke points again — the Mithakhali underpass was closed for 102 minutes after just 0.55 inches of rain, and five underpasses in total (including SG Highway, Shahibaug, Parimal and Vatva GIDC/Vastral) saw closures.
alerts.impact: Continue routing FM/LM vehicles away from Mithakhali, SG Highway, Shahibaug and Vatva GIDC underpasses during rain windows; expect recurring short-duration (60-120 min) closures rather than multi-day disruption.

alerts.title: Kerala: monsoon toll rises to 9 (5 Malappuram, 2 each Kottayam/Idukki) after fresh Kottayam landslide kills tourist; orange alert across six districts, fishing banned
alerts.summary: Kerala's combined monsoon toll has climbed to 9 confirmed dead — 5 in Malappuram (Nilambur flash flood), 2 in Kottayam (including a fresh landslide at Velathusseri near Teekoy on Sep 21 that killed a Tamil Nadu tourist) and 2 in Idukki (Vattavada landslide). IMD orange alert remains in force for Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam and Thrissur — Kottayam and Idukki were both upgraded to orange on Sep 21 — and a statewide fishing ban continues.
alerts.impact: Statewide caution across all orange-alert districts — hold non-essential LM movement in low-lying and hill-adjacent pincodes, verify addresses before dispatch, and keep buffer stock at Kochi/Thrissur/Kottayam hubs until the alert is downgraded.

alerts.title: Kerala: landslide buries plantation shed at Kottakamboor, Vattavada (Idukki High Ranges), kills two named plantation workers
alerts.summary: A landslide struck Kottakamboor in Vattavada (Devikulam taluk, Idukki) around 5pm Sep 20, killing garlic-farming workers Balakrishnan and Chinnu while sheltering from rain; a third worker was critically injured. No further slope collapse has been reported since, but the hillside remains unstable.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk — Idukki High Ranges (Vattavada, Pampadumchola, Kottakamboor, Kadavari route): flag as high landslide-risk, hold non-essential LM movement on hill roads during active rain, and pre-position buffer stock at the Munnar/Idukki hub.

alerts.title: Kerala: Nilambur flash-flood toll rises to 5 named victims; search for missing Sajitha continues at Kottapuzha river
alerts.summary: The Sep 20 flash flood on the Kottapuzha river (Ularvattam-TK Colony stretch, between Chokkad and Amarambalam panchayats, Nilambur) swept away several people without any local rainfall trigger — traced to a sudden upstream surge. The confirmed toll has risen to 5 (Muhammed Kutty, Anas, Rahim, Sajjad and Rafiq); Sajitha of TK Colony, who was washing clothes riverside, remains missing. Fire Force and police resumed the search Sep 22 after strong currents halted Monday's operation.
alerts.impact: Flag Nilambur/Malappuram river-adjacent pincodes and forest-catchment-fed streams for flash-flood risk even absent local rain — hold LM movement near riverside routes and verify road conditions before dispatch into Nilambur taluk.

alerts.title: Karnataka: Agumbe Ghat (NH-169A) heavy-vehicle ban stays in force through September 30 on landslide risk
alerts.summary: Udupi's Deputy Commissioner has kept the Section 115 MV Act order banning heavy vehicles on NH-169A's Agumbe Ghat stretch in force until September 30 due to landslide risk; heavy vehicles are diverted via Thirthahalli-Nagar-Kundapur-Udupi. IMD also continues to flag thunderstorm/lightning risk over Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and Shivamogga, keeping slope-stability watch active for these Malnad districts.
alerts.impact: Standing routing constraint — avoid heavy-vehicle linehaul on Agumbe Ghat through Sep 30; use the Thirthahalli-Nagar-Kundapur-Udupi diversion for the Shivamogga-Udupi corridor FM/LM until the ban lifts.

alerts.title: Karnataka: coastal/Malnad rain (Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru) forecast to ease significantly after Sep 25
alerts.summary: IMD Bengaluru's heavy rain alert for the coastal and Malnad regions — Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and the Shivamogga belt — is now trending toward only scattered light rain/drizzle, with forecasters calling for a significant decrease after Sep 25. Bengaluru itself continues to see cloudy skies and evening showers only.
alerts.impact: Downgrading watch — minor slip-risk remains for Malnad/coastal ghat sections (Charmadi, Shiradi) alongside the existing Agumbe ban, but limited direct LM impact expected in Bengaluru city through the week.

alerts.title: Tamil Nadu: heavy rain across 21 districts (Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Thanjavur, Madurai) easing but moderate rain persists Sep 22
alerts.summary: The Regional Meteorological Centre's heavy-rain forecast for 21 Tamil Nadu districts — Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Dindigul, Thanjavur, Nagapattinam, Madurai, Cuddalore, Vellore, Tiruchirappalli and others — driven by a low-pressure area over the north Andaman Sea, is easing statewide from Sep 22, though moderate rain with 40-50 kmph winds continues over Chennai and roughly a dozen districts plus the Western Ghats.
alerts.impact: Route watch downgrading — hill-taluka (Nilgiris, Dindigul) and low-lying delta pincodes (Thanjavur, Nagapattinam) should see improving conditions through the week; monitor Chennai for residual waterlogging through Sep 22-23.

alerts.title: Telangana: red alert for 11 districts (Asifabad to Hanamkonda) as heavy-to-extremely-heavy rain warning extends through Sep 27 with Bay of Bengal system nearing landfall
alerts.summary: IMD Hyderabad has issued a red alert for Komuram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalapally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanamkonda districts, with an orange alert for the wider north/east Telangana belt, as heavy-to-very-heavy rain (64.4-204.4mm) continues through Sep 27, tied to the Bay of Bengal system intensifying toward deep-depression stage ahead of its Visakhapatnam-Gopalpur landfall late Sep 23. Very heavy to extremely heavy rain is likely at isolated places in Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalapally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanamkonda on Sep 23, shifting to Asifabad, Mancherial and Karimnagar on Sep 24.
alerts.impact: Pre-position buffer stock in the Warangal-Karimnagar-Khammam belt ahead of Sep 23; Hyderabad already saw waterlogging Sep 21-22 (Kapra, Musheerabad) from early rain bands — expect further delays through Sep 27.

alerts.title: Tamil Nadu: fishermen advised off Gulf of Mannar and Comorin Sea as squally winds up to 55 kmph forecast
alerts.summary: IMD has forecast squally winds of up to 55 kmph over the Gulf of Mannar, adjoining south Tamil Nadu coast and Comorin Sea, and has advised fishermen against venturing into these waters.
alerts.impact: Coastal Tamil Nadu FM pickups (Tuticorin, Kanyakumari, Ramanathapuram belt) should expect minor delays tied to rough-sea conditions; no port closures reported yet.

alerts.title: Bay of Bengal deep depression (potential Cyclone 'Arnab') tracking toward Visakhapatnam-Gopalpur landfall late Sep 23; red alert widens to Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Rayagada, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram
alerts.summary: As of 8:30am IST Sep 22, the system was centred about 200km SE of Gopalpur (Odisha), 200km ESE of Kalingapatnam (AP), 210km south of Puri and 290km east of Visakhapatnam, and is forecast to cross the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur late Wednesday night (Sep 23) or early Thursday (Sep 24) as a deep depression, with winds of 55-65 kmph gusting to 70-75 kmph. It has not yet been officially named 'Arnab' (proposed by Bangladesh) — naming only occurs if it reaches cyclonic-storm strength. Red alert now covers Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput and Rayagada in Odisha and Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam in Andhra Pradesh for extremely heavy rain on Sep 22-23; Odisha has closed schools/anganwadis in vulnerable districts, cancelled government staff leave, restricted ghat roads and Chilika ferry services, and fishermen along Odisha/AP/WB coasts are barred from the sea through at least Sep 25.
alerts.impact: Pre-position for landfall — Ganjam/Puri/Gajapati/Koraput/Rayagada (Odisha) and Srikakulam/Vizianagaram/Visakhapatnam (AP) hubs should pre-build 3-4 day buffer stock, suspend fishing-belt LM attempts, and prepare to flag NS for low-lying coastal pincodes from Sep 22 evening through Sep 24. Telangana, AP interior, West Bengal coastal and Jharkhand southern/eastern hubs should expect wind/rain-related delays through Sep 26-27.

alerts.title: Odisha: villages remain marooned in Sundargarh's Bonai block as Sarasara, Patang bridges near Balang stay submerged
alerts.summary: At least five villages remain marooned in Sundargarh district's Bonai block after the Sarasara and Patang bridges near Balang stayed submerged; no confirmation of bridge clearance has surfaced. Pre-build buffer stock at Rourkela hub given the compounding cyclone landfall expected Sep 23-24.
alerts.impact: Flag Bonai block villages non-serviceable until bridges are confirmed clear; pre-build buffer stock at Rourkela hub given the compounding cyclone landfall on Sep 23-24.

alerts.title: Odisha: Malkangiri floodwaters recede and NH-326 reopens, but district sits directly in the incoming cyclone system's red-alert zone
alerts.summary: Floodwaters that had submerged the Kanyashram, Poteru, Pangam and Kankurukonda bridges and halted NH-326 traffic have receded, and vehicular movement has resumed with normal life returning per local reports. However, Malkangiri and the wider Koraput-Rayagada belt now sit within the red-alert zone for the incoming Bay of Bengal deep depression, raising fresh flood-recurrence risk for Sep 23-24.
alerts.impact: NH-326 is passable for now — resume standard FM/LM routing but keep contingency buffer ready given the compounding cyclone-linked rain arriving Sep 23-24.

alerts.title: Jharkhand: flash-flood alert re-escalates across 14 districts as the same Bay of Bengal system brings fresh rain through Sep 26
alerts.summary: IMD's flash-flood alert, tied to the Bay of Bengal system also affecting Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, covers a yellow alert for 11 districts and heightened risk in southern/eastern Jharkhand through Sep 26 as the system tracks inland after its Sep 23-24 landfall.
alerts.impact: Pre-position buffer stock at Ranchi/Jamshedpur hubs and flag southern/eastern Jharkhand pincodes for likely LM delay through Sep 26.

alerts.title: Jharkhand: Ganga flood in Sahibganj floods Bhartiya Colony, Rasoolpur; Udhwa erosion sweeps away school and homes
alerts.summary: The Ganga is flowing roughly 57cm above the danger mark at Sahibganj, flooding Bhartiya Colony and Rasoolpur localities; separately, erosion in Udhwa block has destroyed homes and a school building in the Ganga diyara belt.
alerts.impact: Flag Sahibganj town (Bhartiya Colony, Rasoolpur) and Udhwa diyara-belt pincodes non-serviceable; verify riverside addresses before LM dispatch and monitor for further erosion through the week.

alerts.title: Bihar: Ganga flood receding at most stations after record-breaking levels, but Bhagalpur embankment breaches still under repair
alerts.summary: The Ganga, which broke its all-time high-water record at multiple gauge stations including Gandhi Ghat, Patna, is now receding at most stations, with the Son river also receding. Embankment breaches near Bhagalpur remain under repair, with more than 47 lakh people affected across several districts per the latest confirmed figures.
alerts.impact: Bhagalpur diyara/embankment-breach panchayats remain non-serviceable until breach repairs complete; maintain buffer for Bhagalpur/Patna-hub linehaul as relief operations continue.

alerts.title: West Bengal: Padma erosion swallows 19 houses and Manasa temple overnight in Radhakrishnapur village, Raghunathganj (Murshidabad)
alerts.summary: Overnight Padma-river erosion at Radhakrishnapur village (Raghunathganj, Murshidabad) swallowed 19 houses and the local Manasa temple, displacing families to Sekalipur flood shelter. Other affected Murshidabad blocks include Farakka, Samserganj, Suti I/II, Lalgola, Bhagawangola I/II, Raninagar I/II and Jalangi; irrigation officials expect erosion to continue through end-September.
alerts.impact: Serviceability loss — flag Radhakrishnapur and surrounding Raghunathganj/Farakka/Samserganj riverside pincodes non-serviceable, verify addresses before dispatch, and monitor for further overnight bank loss through end-September.

alerts.title: West Bengal: fresh Ganga erosion in Malda's Manikchak sweeps away roughly 50 houses near Shantimor/Gopalpur; Farakka Barrage discharging 10-11.5 lakh cusecs
alerts.summary: Fresh Ganga erosion in Malda's Manikchak block has washed away roughly 50 houses near Shantimor/Gopalpur, with Kaliachak I & II and Ratua I & II blocks also affected; West Ratanpur Primary School lost 6 of 8 classrooms and nine schools in the district have suspended classes. All 69 gates of the Farakka/Indrapuri Barrage have been opened, discharging 10-11.5 lakh cusecs, and ₹3,600 crore has been allotted for anti-erosion works across Malda, Murshidabad and Nadia.
alerts.impact: Flag Manikchak (Shantimor, Gopalpur), Kaliachak and Ratua riverside pincodes non-serviceable; expect erosion-driven road/school access loss to continue through end-September as barrage discharge stays high.

alerts.title: West Bengal: Mangtabong village (Yuksom, West Sikkim border) landslide damage persists; Darjeeling-Kalimpong hills face fresh slope-stability scrutiny after the Nepal Himalayan mega-disaster
alerts.summary: Heavy overnight rain on Sep 18 triggered a landslide at Mangtabong village (Tsong Dubdi Ward) near Yuksom Bazar, damaging houses and killing livestock; Kalimpong district administration continues to advise avoiding NH-10 during heavy rain in favor of alternate routes. Separately, a Sep 22 EastMojo ground analysis warns that the underlying geology of Darjeeling/Kalimpong (fractured Daling-group rock, clogged hill jhoras, hill-cut road construction) makes the region prone to compound landslide events like the October 2025 disaster (493 concurrent slides, dozens killed, NH-10/NH-55 severed) — a risk being reassessed regionally following the catastrophic Aug 26 Langtang Lirung glacier-collapse flood disaster in Nepal (1,400+ dead, 6,000+ missing) that also raises transboundary flood-surge concern for Teesta-corridor settlements downstream in Sikkim/Darjeeling.
alerts.impact: Route watch — Darjeeling-Kalimpong hill pincodes, the Yuksom/West Sikkim border belt, the NH-10 corridor and Teesta-riverside settlements: keep buffer time for LM/linehaul, verify addresses before dispatch, and treat this as a standing structural risk area rather than a one-off event, especially once South Bengal's incoming Bay-of-Bengal-driven heavy rain arrives Sep 22-25.

alerts.title: West Bengal: orange alert for South/North 24 Parganas, Medinipur, Jhargram, Birbhum, Murshidabad as Bay of Bengal system nears landfall
alerts.summary: IMD's orange alert remains in force for South and North 24 Parganas, East and West Medinipur, Jhargram, Birbhum and Murshidabad from Sep 21, with heavy rain of up to 110mm expected Sep 22-25 in South 24 Parganas and Howrah, tied to the Bay of Bengal system now tracking toward a Visakhapatnam-Gopalpur landfall late Sep 23.
alerts.impact: Pre-position buffer stock in South 24 Parganas, Howrah and coastal Medinipur hubs ahead of Sep 22-25; expect urban waterlogging in Kolkata's low-lying wards during the peak rain window.

alerts.title: Nagaland: NH-702 partially reopens for light vehicles between Changtongya and Longleng, but repeated rockslides keep cutting the road off again
alerts.summary: NH-702 between Changtongya and Longleng has reopened intermittently for light vehicles, but repeated rockslides keep cutting the road off again, per local reporting describing a 'struggle that refuses to end.' The alternate Tangha-Kangching-Merangkong diversion is also unsuitable for heavy vehicles. NHIDCL/contractor clearance work is ongoing.
alerts.impact: Light-parcel LM/FM movement can resume intermittently via NH-702 or the Tangha-Kangching-Merangkong diversion, but hold all heavy-vehicle linehaul and keep buffer stock at the Changtongya gateway until full restoration — treat reopenings as unstable, not final.

alerts.title: Mizoram: Kolasib district landslide risk downgraded to moderate — Vairengte, Saihapui 'K' roads passable, no fresh incident since Sep 14
alerts.summary: A landslide near the Assam border killed 14-year-old Zodingliana and injured four in Vairengte town on Sep 12; precautionary evacuations followed across Kolasib district (Saihapui 'K', North Chawnpui near the Serlui 'B' hydro dam, Khuangpuilam locality, Pangbalkawn), and Sialsuk villagers sheltered 500+ stranded travellers cut off by disrupted roads. No fresh incident has been reported since Sep 14, but renewed rain spillover from the incoming Bay of Bengal system is a risk factor.
alerts.impact: Downgrading from high to moderate — Kolasib district roads are passable for now; keep contingency routing ready and monitor for renewed evacuation orders if rain intensifies again this week.

alerts.title: Sikkim: one-way traffic restored at Bardang (20th Mile) on NH-10 after Sep 16-17 mudslide, but slope remains 'sensitive'
alerts.summary: One-way traffic has been restored at Bardang (20th Mile) on NH-10 after the Sep 16-17 mudslide; 12 households were affected and relief of roughly Rs 2.7 lakh has been disbursed. The broader Rangpo subdivision saw multiple landslides in the same spell, including a vehicle briefly trapped and later freed; the Bardang stretch remains flagged as 'sensitive' due to continued water accumulation and soft soil, so restoration is ongoing, not complete.
alerts.impact: NH-10 traffic is moving one-way through Bardang — build in delay buffer for Sikkim-bound linehaul and avoid the stretch during active rain given the still-sensitive slope.

alerts.title: Arunachal Pradesh: Zemithang-Tawang road blocked near Shakti village; Balipara-Chariduar-Tawang highway also repeatedly hit in West Kameng
alerts.summary: A landslide near Shakti village blocked the Zemithang-Tawang road in early September; the Balipara-Chariduar-Tawang (BCT) highway in West Kameng has also been repeatedly hit by slides this monsoon. Neither corridor has a confirmed full-restoration report — this is a recurring pattern typical of both routes.
alerts.impact: Flag Zemithang-Tawang and BCT highway corridors for intermittent LM/FM disruption; keep buffer stock at Tawang/Bomdila gateway hubs and avoid time-critical dispatches on these roads during active rain.

alerts.title: Assam: Brahmaputra erosion swallows Bhakat Chapori (Majuli, 16 villages threatened) and Balijan tea garden, part of a decade-long crisis displacing 23,000+ families
alerts.summary: Brahmaputra erosion is actively swallowing Bhakat Chapori in Majuli (16 villages plus lower Majuli threatened) and Balijan tea garden in Chabua, reportedly overtaking geo-bag protection within a day of placement. This is part of a chronic, decade-long crisis that has devoured 330 villages and displaced over 23,000 families across Assam, not a one-off event.
alerts.impact: Flag Majuli island and Chabua tea-garden-belt pincodes for standing erosion risk — verify riverside addresses before dispatch and maintain alternate ferry/road routing for Majuli given its island geography.

alerts.title: Manipur: Mapithel dam gate release flooded Thoubal river basin villages, kills two elderly residents
alerts.summary: Four gates of the Mapithel dam were suddenly opened on Sep 14, flooding downstream Thoubal river basin villages — inundating paddy fields, fish farms and households; two elderly residents were swept away and died. The Manipur High Court has taken cognisance of recurring floods and landslides tied to dam management practices and deforestation in the basin. No fresh gate-release incident reported since, but the risk factor stands given the state's ongoing unrest and unrelated Bay of Bengal rain spillover.
alerts.impact: Flag Thoubal river basin villages downstream of Mapithel dam for flash-flood risk whenever gate releases occur — coordinate with local sources on release schedules where possible and avoid dispatch during active release windows.

alerts.title: Sikkim: Rimbi and Singlitam (Gyalshing district) landslide-evacuated families remain displaced, ICDS centre flood-hit
alerts.summary: Incessant rain since Sep 14 intensified a landslide threat at Rimbi (128 people, 28 households evacuated to the Rimbi Gram Panchayat Kendra) and Singlitam (7 families, 33+ people moved to a relief shelter) in West Sikkim's Gyalshing district. Debris has piled up along the Nik Kholsa stream near Mandir Point, sending debris-laden water toward Rimbi village during heavy rain, and the Rimbi ICDS centre below the slide zone has flooded, prompting officials to consider relocating it. No source confirms full resolution as of Sep 22.
alerts.impact: Flag Rimbi and Singlitam (Gyalshing district, West Sikkim) as high landslide-risk, non-serviceable during active rain — verify road access before LM dispatch and route via alternate Gyalshing-town approaches where available.
